title: Traffic Split Composer & Rollback Autopilot
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Implement a robust, declarative composer and enforcement layer for canary rollouts that supports traffic-splits, step schedules, shadowing, A/B tests and automated rollback. The feature must be usable from both the Console and the API, store auditable configs (gitops-compatible), and provide deterministic simulation and safety checks before apply.

Background: Current rollout primitives exist in ad-hoc form in several places (console UI, runtime flags). We need a single source-of-truth rollout config that:
- expresses weighted traffic splits across model variants and region/capacity tiers,
- supports step schedules (time-based and metric-based),
- integrates shadow traffic for offline evaluation,
- supports A/B allocations with metric tracking, and
- drives an autopilot that can trigger rollbacks when guardrails are violated.

Design decisions and trade-offs discussed: 
- DSL vs JSON Schema: we will expose a JSON Schema for machine consumption and a human-friendly YAML alias in Console. Chosen because it is easier to validate and to store in S3/Git snapshots.
- Strict vs permissive guardrails: start with conservative defaults (P95 latency + error-rate + custom eval regression) and allow tenant overrides. Conservative defaults reduce outages at the cost of slower rollouts.
- Runtime enforcement: rollout decisions will be evaluated by a central rollout controller service (stateless) that reads configs and issues route updates to the router. This avoids coupling rollout logic to every node.

Key components to deliver in this ticket: 
1) Traffic Split Composer (API + Console UX): declarative config that maps model variants to weighted routes with matchers (region, capacity tier, tenant). Support fraction-of-requests and absolute-headroom.
2) Step Scheduler: support both fixed-time steps and metric gates (e.g., hold for 30m or until latency delta < 5%).
3) Guardrail Engine: configurable predicates (latency p95 delta > 10%, error-rate increase > 0.5%, eval-score regression > 1%) with severity tags and cooldown windows.
4) Rollback Autopilot: automatic rollback orchestration that triggers safe fallback variant or full rollback and creates audit events + alerting.
5) Shadowing & A/B hooks: allow sending 100% shadowed traffic to non-responding variants for offline scoring; track A/B cohorts with per-variant metrics.
6) Simulation & Dry-run CLI: rollout simulator (local/CI) to validate config against historical traffic traces and detect potential failures (e.g., incompatible fallback, overflow on KV cache).
7) Observability: per-rollout dashboard, event timeline, token-level cost delta estimate, and a small set of SLO checks used by guardrails.

Acceptance criteria: 
- API and JSON schema published, with at least two example templates (time-based canary and metric-gated canary).
- Console UX wireframes implemented for config creation and a dry-run preview.
- Rollout controller can apply a 3-step canary (1%, 20%, 100%) to a test tenant and automatically rollback on simulated P95 spike.
- Audit logs and rollout events appear in the Console timeline and are retained per tenant policy.
- Unit & integration tests cover simulation, guardrail evaluation, and rollback paths.

Backward compatibility: rollout configs default to legacy router semantics when only a single variant is specified. Migration doc will be provided for teams with YAML/JSON examples.

Operational runbook (summary): 
- On guardrail breach, controller issues immediate rollback and marks rollout as FAILED.
- An incident ticket template is created automatically including metrics snapshot and the rollout config snapshot.
- For repeated noisy signals, controller will escalate to on-call after 3 rollouts in 24h.

Open questions: 
- Exact thresholds for default guardrails (proposed in design doc, need PM sign-off).
- Storage model for config versioning (S3 + Dynamo index vs Postgres).
- How to express complex cohort matching (headers, JWT claims) without exposing too much runtime complexity.

Migration plan and rollout: 
- Stage 1 (internal alpha): CLI and API for test tenants + simulator.
- Stage 2 (beta): Console form + rollout controller enabled for a small set of customers under feature flag.
- Stage 3 (GA): On by default with a migration tool to convert legacy flags.

Related artifacts and references included in links field.
